text:
Marissa Cole: quick alignment thread on route-level A/B testing beta. We need to lock: (1) beta gating/tier + who gets enabled, (2) pricing/packaging implications (esp evals), (3) “must-have” metrics in v1 for Console results.

Marissa Cole: current proposal: Console-first workflow, feature-flagged. Beta = Hosted + Dedicated only. Private follow-on. Thoughts?

Dylan Brooks: +1 on feature flag + entitlement check. We can ship the UI behind `console_ab_testing_beta` and hard-disable if telemetry isn’t live.

Paula Mendes: gating should also be “telemetry readiness”. If exposure logs + cost attribution aren’t in prod, results UI is misleading.

Logan Wright: yep. I’d like a hard dependency: exposure event ingestion + daily aggregation jobs in place before we enable anyone external.

Tessa Morgan: design side: if we’re gating, we need copy that explains why the tab isn’t visible / “ask your admin” vs a broken experience. Also: beta badge + limitations banner.

Kenji Nakamura: also need to decide if “Results” shows confidence indicators in beta or just “directional”. I’m worried we’ll over-promise stats rigor.

Marissa Cole: on that: for beta we can label it “beta results (directional)” but we still need baseline metrics.

Nadia Rahman: packaging question: cost metrics are sensitive. Are we promising “$ per 1k tokens” or “estimated cost” vs actual billed? Metering is tricky across Dedicated.

Paula Mendes: I’d prefer we show “token + GPU attribution” in beta, not “billing numbers”. Wording: “estimated compute cost” and “token usage” with clear disclaimers.

Dylan Brooks: +1. Console can display: input_tokens/output_tokens, total_tokens, TTFT, e2e latency, error rate. We can add “estimated GPU-seconds” if available, but avoid calling it invoice.

Sean Gallagher: jumping in from SRE angle: beta gating MUST include guardrails + rollback path. If we’re letting customers shift traffic, we need (a) max latency regression threshold and (b) error-rate threshold, with alerts routed to oncall + clear runbook.

Marissa Cole: agreed. We’ll keep “auto rollback” as phase 2? But at least manual rollback and guardrail alert in beta.

Connor O'Brien: release train note: we should not enable beta flag until gateway exposure events + metrics tags are in all regions. Otherwise we’ll have partial reporting. Suggest: ship code dark, then flip region by region.

Priya Natarajan: from platform: Dedicated is fine if routing policy precedence is clear. Private is a separate can of worms (customer-managed telemetry pipelines). I’m in favor of Hosted+Dedicated beta, Private later with explicit requirements.

Kenji Nakamura: can we get clarity on which metrics are “v1 required” vs “nice to have” so design can prioritize layout? I’m working on dashboard components.

Marissa Cole: let’s define “must have” for v1:
- Exposure volume by variant (requests, streaming vs non-streaming counts)
- p50/p95/p99 end-to-end latency
- TTFT p50/p95 (at minimum)
- Error rate by variant (breakout 4xx/5xx/timeouts; highlight 429)
- Token usage by variant (input/output/total)
- Estimated cost deltas (token + compute attribution, clearly labeled)

Marissa Cole: “nice to have / phase 2”: per-region filters, per-model breakdown when multiple models in a variant, drilldown traces, quality metrics w/ CI.

Logan Wright: on “must have”: we should also display “assignment stickiness key present” / coverage. If customers don’t send the hash header, they’ll see variant flapping + weird metrics.

Paula Mendes: +1. We can show “% requests assigned deterministically” as a health indicator. Or at least warn when `x-redwood-experiment-key` missing.

Dylan Brooks: we can add a validation step in create flow: “Detected eligible identifier” vs “will fall back to api_key stickiness” and show impact.

Tessa Morgan: UX idea: pre-flight checklist before “Start experiment”:
1) Telemetry enabled
2) Variant configs validate (no overlapping canary)
3) Stickiness key configured
4) Guardrails acknowledged

Tessa Morgan: and a strong warning copy: “This will shift production traffic.”

Nadia Rahman: pricing/packaging: do we treat A/B testing as a paid add-on? If it’s in base tier, support load will spike. If it’s enterprise-only, we need a story for PLG users.

Marissa Cole: current thinking: beta is free but gated (design partners + request access). For GA: Hosted Pro gets basic A/B (2 variants, limited retention), Enterprise gets advanced (more variants, longer retention, audit exports). “Evals attachment” might be enterprise add-on.

Priya Natarajan: that sounds consistent with other Console features. Please make sure entitlement checks can handle “A/B basic” vs “A/B + evals”.

Paula Mendes: metrics retention is a big lever for packaging. If we store raw exposure logs longer for enterprise, that’s cost. Suggest: beta retention 7 days; GA basic 14; enterprise 30/90.

Logan Wright: +1. Also sampling policy: exposure logs might be sampled, but aggregated metrics should be complete (or at least explain sampling). We should be explicit in UI: “Exposure events may be sampled; latency/cost metrics are aggregated from gateway metrics.”

Kenji Nakamura: noted. I’ll add a small “About these metrics” panel in results.

Sean Gallagher: please include “guardrail status” in results: e.g., “Latency regression +12% vs threshold 10%” and a one-click rollback action (even if manual) with audit trail.

Dylan Brooks: we can wire “Rollback” button to the existing rollout stop workflow. Needs audit log events: start/stop/rollback. (Marcus/Naomi will want this anyway.)

Marissa Cole: action items:
- Marissa: write up beta gating + packaging proposal (basic vs advanced + evals) and share for review.
- Paula/Logan/Nadia: confirm the v1 metrics list + exact definitions (esp TTFT + cost labeling) so design can finalize.
- Dylan/Connor: dependency list for flipping the beta flag (regions + telemetry readiness).
- Tessa/Kenji: incorporate pre-flight checklist + “directional results” disclaimers in the flow.

Marissa Cole: also dropping links for context:
- Linear: PM-481
- Design: DES-142 / DES-143
- Docs draft: redwood-docs PR #2217

Tessa Morgan: :thumbsup: I’ll update prototypes w/ the pre-flight step and send for async comments.

Logan Wright: I’ll post a short spec snippet on required metric definitions + what’s sampled vs not.

Sean Gallagher: and I’ll send proposed beta guardrail thresholds + alert routing requirements. We should not enable external orgs without that.

Marissa Cole: perfect. thanks all.
